# Events & Cancellation

| Feature | Status | Caveats | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EventTarget` / `addEventListener` / `dispatchEvent` | ✅ | | • Node's own (`lib/internal/event_target.js`) written in TypeScript (`lib/node/kml_event_target.ts`), reached as a global without an import ([ADR-01203](../adr/ADR-01203.md)): `addEventListener` with `once`/`passive`/`capture`/`signal` and a `handleEvent` object, duplicate suppression, `removeEventListener`, `dispatchEvent` returning `!defaultPrevented`; a listener's throw is reported through `process.nextTick` as an uncaught exception while the dispatch goes on; `class X extends EventTarget` works |
| `Event` / `CustomEvent` | ✅ | | • `type`, `bubbles`, `cancelable`, `composed`, `defaultPrevented`, `timeStamp`, `isTrusted`, `target`/`currentTarget`/`srcElement`, `eventPhase`, `returnValue`, `cancelBubble`, `composedPath()`, `preventDefault()` (a no-op on a non-cancelable event or in a passive listener), `stopPropagation()`, `stopImmediatePropagation()`, the phase constants; `CustomEvent.detail` (`null` by default); both subclassable ([ADR-01203](../adr/ADR-01203.md)) |
| `AbortController` / `AbortSignal` | ✅ | • DOMException carries no legacy numeric `.code`<br>• `JSON.stringify` of an error-subclass `abort(reason)` yields `{}` — Node serializes the instance's own enumerable fields (an assigned `this.name`, extra declared fields); needs per-field enumerability, same residue as `allSettled` ([TDD-00222](../tdd/TDD-00222.md)) | • Node's `lib/internal/abort_controller.js` in TypeScript, subclasses of `EventTarget` ([ADR-01203](../adr/ADR-01203.md)): `aborted`, `reason`, `throwIfAborted()`, a trusted `abort` event, `onabort` holding its listener slot from its first assignment, `AbortSignal.abort()`/`timeout()` (an unref'd timer)/`any()`; `new AbortSignal()` is Node's `TypeError: Illegal constructor`<br>• `signal.reason` is `any` ([ADR-01004](../adr/ADR-01004.md)): a never-aborted signal reads `undefined`, `abort(reason)` preserves any value's type (`typeof`, `===`), and the default/timeout DOMExceptions keep their full Error shape (`.name`/`.message`/`String`/`instanceof`) through the box via the field-0 type-id ([TDD-00222](../tdd/TDD-00222.md))<br>• `fetch(url, { signal })` cancellation works — pre-flight, mid-flight, and via **`AbortSignal.timeout(ms)`**, on both the top-level `await` path and the fiber path (a fetch awaited inside an `http.listen` handler): the await loop checks the signal every spin, and the event loop folds the timeout deadline into its `select()` wait so an idle loop wakes at the deadline — then tears the transfer down and rejects with **`signal.reason`** itself, Node parity ([ADR-01004](../adr/ADR-01004.md)): the default is a `DOMException` (`instanceof DOMException` and, since it inherits `Error`, `instanceof Error` both hold), named `AbortError` for a manual abort and `TimeoutError` for a timeout, and a custom `abort(reason)` value is rethrown as-is ([ADR-00237](../adr/ADR-00237.md)–[ADR-00240](../adr/ADR-00240.md))<br>• `new DOMException(message?, name?)` is constructible directly |
